answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to pass through a prism of multi-party computation checks that verify unique hardware fingerprints. Participants then stake tokens in a shared lotus pool whose growth depends on honest attestations, while a rotating lantern beacon periodically challenges random agents to re-prove liveness. This combination of fingerprinting, economic bonding, and ongoing challenges raises the cost of creating fake identities far above any potential reward.
